about: Research for embraer.py and fps_embraer.html: five web research tracks (Embraer and Korea, Brazil-US relations, price pressure from a third maker, partner precedents, Korean and Japanese industry), each followed by an adversarial verifier. The verifiers could not open web sources (the session's search budget was used up and many hosts did not resolve), so they checked what they could against the Boeing and Embraer call transcripts, 10-Ks and Airbus's Board Report in the repository: 21 findings confirmed, 16 corrected, 151 could not be checked. Findings rest on search-result extracts unless a verdict says otherwise; each carries its own confidence.

findings.claim: South Korean President Lee Jae Myung publicly named joint development of a next-generation commercial aircraft with Brazil as one of three priority areas for cooperation, at the Korea-Brazil business roundtable in Sao Paulo.
findings.detail: Lee said Brazil 'possesses world-class production capabilities in small and medium-sized commercial aircraft' and told Brazilian officials 'Let's build civilian aircraft together in the future, if possible.' The other two priorities were critical minerals and K-beauty. This came the day after his summit with Lula in Brasilia (state visit 26-29 July 2026). Lee and Lula named Presidential Policy Chief Kim Yong-beom and Brazilian Vice President Geraldo Alckmin as the officials in charge of following up on economic cooperation.
findings.source_title: Korea Herald: Lee calls for joint development of next-generation commercial aircraft (also Korea Times, Korea JoongAng Daily)

findings.claim: Korea's Presidential Policy Chief Kim Yong-beom said Seoul wants to take part in Embraer's planned next-generation airliner from the development stage, but called the talks 'very early stage' and said neither the form of participation nor the commercial terms had been set.
findings.detail: Kim was quoted as saying Embraer 'is drawing up plans to comprehensively upgrade its lineup with next-generation aircraft, so if the conditions are right, we would like to participate.' The same Korea Herald piece says Embraer is considering moving beyond 70-100-seat regional jets into 'midsize aircraft capable of carrying 150 to 200 passengers'. Kim also said Korea was proceeding cautiously because the market is dominated by a few manufacturers such as Airbus and Boeing. The 150-200 seat range comes from the Korean briefing and press, not from an Embraer statement. I saw this only in search-result extracts because koreaherald.com could not be fetched.
findings.source_title: Korea Herald: Korea eyes joint jet development with Embraer (and 'Korea eyes joint aircraft development with Embraer, moving beyond parts supply')

findings.claim: KAI and Embraer signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) on cooperation in civil aviation and aerospace on 28 July 2026 in Sao Paulo, signed by KAI President Kim Jong-chool and Embraer CEO Francisco Gomes Neto.
findings.detail: It was one of seven company MoUs signed at the roundtable. Trade press frames it around aircraft structures: the two firms will explore cooperation across design, engineering, manufacturing and quality control, and identify future areas of collaboration including commercial aircraft and future air mobility. One report notes it sets out no concrete contracts or business scale. Aviator and the Korean presidential office say it builds on a February 2026 announcement that the two would jointly explore a next-generation commercial aircraft. Korea's industry minister attended. The MoU is non-binding, so this is not a launch, a joint venture or a funding commitment.
findings.source_title: Airframer: KAI partners with Embraer on structures; Asia Business Daily; aviator.aero; FlightGlobal 'Embraer, KAI to explore more aerostructure co-operation'

findings.claim: During Lula's state visit to Seoul (summit 23 February 2026), Korea and Brazil raised ties to a strategic partnership with a 2026-2029 action plan, and Lee said he hoped to extend aviation supply-chain links into joint development of next-generation civil aircraft.
findings.detail: Kim Yong-beom's July 2026 briefing said KAI and Embraer had announced cooperation on joint development of a next-generation civil aircraft during Lula's February visit. I could not find the text of that February announcement. Lula was the first Brazilian leader to make a state visit to Korea in 21 years.
findings.source_title: Korea.net: President Lee, Brazil upgrade ties to strategic partnership; UPI

findings.claim: Korean press reports that KAI and Korean Air each held separate talks with Embraer on possibly joining a joint development, and that KAI's CEO wants a strategic partnership that shares technology and risk rather than one-off production work.
findings.detail: Korean reports say KAI's Kim Jong-chool said co-developing with Brazil would reduce the development-cost burden. KAI now supplies wing structures and eVTOL structures to Embraer, and Korean Air supplies fuselage parts. Hanjin Group/Korean Air Chairman Cho Won-tae attended the roundtable and said Korean Air would act as a bridge. No Korean Air-Embraer MoU was reported. Participation and scale are to be set after economic reviews and company negotiations.
findings.source_title: Nate News / Asia Today / Money Today (Korean-language coverage of the Sao Paulo roundtable)

findings.claim: Aviation Week reported that South Korea is looking for a foreign co-developer for its first commercial airliner, with Brazil (Embraer and the Brazilian government) the leading candidate after Lee's state visit.
findings.detail: The article is by Kim Minseok, dated 30 July 2026 and paywalled, so I saw only its opening. A search summary attributed to CAPA mentioned a 200-plus-seat narrowbody with engines led by Hanwha Aerospace, but I could not open it or confirm it; see gaps.
findings.source_title: Aviation Week: South Korea Seeks International Partner For Airliner Program

findings.claim: In May 2024 the Wall Street Journal reported that Embraer was exploring a new narrowbody to challenge Boeing and Airbus and was sounding out partners and backers, including Saudi Arabia's PIF and manufacturers in Turkey, India and South Korea.
findings.detail: The report cited unnamed sources and said the project was at an early stage. Embraer then issued a statement denying plans to develop a new commercial aircraft, while saying it 'certainly has the capability to develop a new narrowbody aircraft' (exact wording seen only second-hand).
findings.source_title: WSJ reprint 'Brazil's Embraer Plots a New 737-Sized Jet to Rival Boeing' (tovima.com); MarketScreener/Reuters summary

findings.claim: The Air Current reported that Saudi Arabia and PIF 'may hold the key' to funding Embraer's possible new airliner, and later that Embraer was also talking to the Japanese government and Japanese heavy industry groups.
findings.detail: Both reports rely on unnamed sources: 'industry officials' for Saudi Arabia and 'two people briefed' for Japan. Neither was confirmed by Embraer, PIF or METI. The Air Current also said Embraer had told it in October (2024) that it was eyeing a 2025 or 2026 decision on its next major product; that slipped. Embraer's actual Saudi deals are defence-related: a SAMI MoU in November 2023, and in 2025 it dropped a Saudi C-390 final-assembly offer in favour of the UAE. A June 2026 Brazilian analysis says the Saudi link has cooled.
findings.source_title: The Air Current: Embraer's search for new airplane partner brings Saudi aviation ambitions to the fore; Japan added to Embraer partners list

findings.claim: Embraer CEO Francisco Gomes Neto told Bloomberg TV that Embraer is 'making studies for a new product, but we don't have any concrete plans yet' and 'We don't have any plans yet to go bigger.'
findings.detail: He said this when asked about a 737 rival. He said the priority was selling E2s and business jets.
findings.source_title: BNN Bloomberg: Embraer CEO says planemaker mulling new jet in hint at 737 rival

findings.claim: In a 2024 Aviation Week interview Gomes Neto said Embraer sees the narrowbody 'window of opportunity' but must understand the scenarios better, does not want to put the company at risk, and would need to be financially very stable to fund any move with partners.
findings.detail: Related coverage at the time said a narrowbody move was unlikely before the next decade.
findings.source_title: Aviation Week: Embraer CEO Sees Narrowbody Window Of Opportunity

findings.claim: Gomes Neto said Embraer will start defining its next product or products from 2030, and that its strategic plan to 2030 contains no concrete larger-aircraft project.
findings.detail: His quote: 'I didn't say that Embraer is considering making a larger plane. What I've been saying is that it is always studying alternatives and new products.' The exact date is uncertain (2024-2025, around Embraer's February 2025 plan for R$20bn of investment and US$10bn revenue by 2030).
findings.source_title: Air Data News: New Embraer aircraft to be launched from 2030 onwards, says CEO; Aerotelegraph

findings.claim: On a first-quarter earnings call, Gomes Neto said any new aircraft launch depends on how mature suppliers' technology is and on a funding strategy that 'doesn't jeopardize the company's financial capacity', with no timeline and no new models expected before 2030.
findings.detail: Embraer is studying technologies for structures, wings, cockpits and propulsion, and has sought financial and industrial partners. A Q1 2025 call summary also said Embraer had no immediate plans to launch a new aircraft. On the Q1 2026 call he said Embraer is investing in new technologies 'to prepare for a future product cycle'.
findings.source_title: Air Data News: New aircraft depend on mature technology and solid funding plan, says Embraer; MarketBeat Q1 2026 call highlights

findings.claim: Embraer cancelled its 70-90-seat next-generation turboprop on 4 November 2025 (CEO: it 'has been cancelled by us') and gave no timeline for a new aircraft: 'We are prepared to make the decision when the time comes.'
findings.detail: The reason reported was immature engine technology; one report says there was also no launch partner or government backing. At Farnborough in July 2026, Commercial Aviation CEO Arjan Meijer said the turboprop was 'completely shelved'. The E175-E2 remains on hold because of US pilot scope clauses. This shows Embraer will drop a programme that lacks an engine or partners.
findings.source_title: FlightGlobal: Embraer cancels next-generation turboprop concept; Aviation Week: Embraer CEO: No New Turboprops Planned

findings.claim: Gomes Neto told the Financial Times the single-aisle market has room for 'three or four' manufacturers, not just two, citing forecasts of about 40,000 new aircraft over two decades, while again ruling out near-term plans for a 737/A320 competitor.
findings.detail: The interview was reported via Reuters and Air Data News. Its exact date is not visible in the results; the Reuters ID suggests 2025.
findings.source_title: Air Data News: Embraer CEO Says Global Jet Market Has Room for More Boeing and Airbus Rivals (FT via Reuters)

findings.claim: The Economist (30 July 2026) said a larger Embraer jet to compete with A320neo/737 MAX would cost about $10 billion and need partners, and reported that Gomes Neto acknowledged both points.
findings.detail: Brazilian coverage of the article says the decision divides opinion inside Embraer, that Gomes Neto is in no hurry, and that Airbus and Boeing hold about 16,000 orders with waits of up to ten years, against under two years for an E2. Bank of America's Ron Epstein said a successful entry would lift Embraer to a new level. I saw only Portuguese-language secondary reports, not the Economist article.
findings.source_title: TrendsCE / O Povo (BBC Brasil) coverage of The Economist 'Forget Airbus and Boeing. Embraer is taking off'

findings.claim: FlightGlobal reported industry estimates that a new airliner would cost Embraer about $10 billion to develop, while Gomes Neto kept a neutral stance on whether the next platform would be a business jet, an airliner or a defence aircraft.
findings.detail: The figure is an industry estimate, not an Embraer number. The article is about 510 days old, so roughly mid-2025.
findings.source_title: FlightGlobal: Embraer chief Gomes-Neto maintains neutral stance on next aircraft platform

findings.claim: Korean press, reporting the launch of 'Team Korea', said developing one mid-size civil aircraft type takes about 15 trillion won (roughly $10-11 billion), which is why Korea is starting with international co-development.
findings.detail: The report describes Korea's plan as building technology and credibility through international joint development first, and developing its own airliner only in the long term.
findings.source_title: Nate News exclusive: Korea to join Boeing/Airbus as partner, 'goal of independent airliner development'

findings.claim: Airbus CEO Guillaume Faury said Embraer should 'think twice' before entering the narrowbody market against Airbus, Boeing and COMAC, calling it 'a big risk'.
findings.detail: In the same interview Faury said Airbus plans to choose an engine for its A320 successor in 2027, launch around 2030 and enter service in 2037 or 2038. Air Data News dates its report to 26 June 2026.
findings.source_title: Air Data News: Airbus CEO says Embraer should think twice before entering narrowbody market (from Aviation Week interview)

findings.claim: Leeham News (4 September 2026) says Embraer's leadership has given no strong signal whether its next clean-sheet aircraft will be a business jet or a large airliner, and that analysts are split.
findings.detail: Some analysts call a narrowbody a bet-the-company move and cite Bombardier's C Series. Others say Embraer's growth and low debt could absorb a misstep.
findings.source_title: Leeham News: Will Embraer Go Big by Developing a Large Narrowbody Jet?

findings.claim: Embraer's 2025 revenue was a record $7.58 billion (up 18%), with net income of $351.9 million and adjusted EBIT of $656.8 million (8.7% margin). Its 2026 guidance is $8.2-8.5 billion revenue, 80-85 commercial jets and 160-170 business jets.
findings.detail: In August 2026 (Q2 results) the 2026 free-cash-flow target, excluding Eve, was raised from at least $200 million to at least $400 million, with the EBIT margin guided at 10.0-10.6%. Year-end 2025 cash: a Q4 call summary cites standalone net cash of about $109 million, against consolidated net debt of $439 million at Q3 2025 (the two are not directly comparable).
findings.source_title: Embraer 4Q25 earnings release (SEC 6-K); Forecast International Flight Plan

findings.claim: Embraer's backlog reached a record $35.7 billion at the end of Q3 2026: Commercial $15.8bn, Executive $8.2bn, Defence $6.1bn (up 56% on a year earlier), Services $5.6bn.
findings.detail: Q3 2026: 66 deliveries in total, 22 of them commercial; 175 in the first nine months. 36 firm E2 orders in the quarter (Abra 20 E195-E2, ANA 8 more E190-E2), 72 E2 firm orders year to date, commercial book-to-bill 1.2x. Market value was about $11-13 billion in June-September 2026 ($10.97bn on 18 June; about $12.2bn at the end of July).
findings.source_title: AeroTime: Embraer reaches record company-wide backlog of $35.7 billion; StockAnalysis / CompaniesMarketCap

findings.claim: Embraer delivered 78 commercial jets in 2025 (44 E2 and 34 first-generation E-Jets), up from 73 in 2024. It aims for up to about 100 commercial deliveries in 2027 and capacity of about 110-120 commercial jets a year by 2030.
findings.detail: The 110-120 a year by 2030 figure comes from Gomes Neto (Bloomberg Linea, Reuters); the 100 in 2027 ambition comes from a Bloomberg interview on 13 May 2026. Supply-chain shortages, especially engines and fuselage parts, are the main limit on the ramp.
findings.source_title: Air Data News: Embraer ends 2025 with 78 commercial jets delivered; Bloomberg: Embraer sees higher fuel prices driving demand for smaller jets; Bloomberg Linea

findings.claim: Embraer's highest commercial output has been about 100-130 aircraft a year (roughly 9-11 a month): 130 commercial aircraft in 2007, 108 commercial jets in 2016 and 101 E-Jets in 2017.
findings.detail: The 2007 total includes all commercial types (E-Jets plus the remaining ERJ-145s). The first-generation E-Jet entered service in March 2004, so it reached about 10 a month within about three years.
findings.source_title: FlightGlobal: Embraer hits target with 169 deliveries in 2007; FlightGlobal: Embraer targets 100 E-Jet deliveries annually by 2028

findings.claim: The first-generation E-Jet (E170/190) was launched at the Paris Air Show on 14 June 1999 and entered service on 17 March 2004 with LOT, about five years from launch to service, with 16 risk-sharing partners.
findings.detail: One Brazilian source puts the planned investment at $850 million. It is a single uncorroborated source.
findings.source_title: Wikipedia: Embraer E-Jet family; aviacaocomercial.net

findings.claim: The E2 was launched in June 2013 with a $1.7 billion budget; the E190-E2 was certified on 28 February 2018 and entered service with Wideroe on 24 April 2018, which Embraer says was on time and on budget.
findings.detail: The 'on time, on budget' claim comes from Embraer and was not independently audited. Sales have been slow: the E2 passed 500 firm orders only in Q2 2026, 13 years after launch. An Embraer Q1 2026 table shows E195-E2 at 424 firm orders and 169 delivered, and E190-E2 at 65 and 34, which I sum to about 489 firm and 203 delivered. The E175-E2 is on hold past 2027 because of US scope clauses. Reuters reported Embraer saw the main E2 (GTF) engine issues as solved.
findings.source_title: Wikipedia: Embraer E-Jet E2 family; AIN (2016) on $1.7bn budget; Panabee on 500-order milestone

findings.claim: The C-390/KC-390 had 62 orders and 16 deliveries as of September 2026, with NATO and EU buyers including Portugal, Hungary, the Czech Republic, the Netherlands, Austria and Sweden, plus South Korea, Uzbekistan, the UAE (up to 20, May 2026) and Greece (up to 6, November 2026).
findings.detail: The totals are a Wikipedia tally (47 in January 2026, 62 in September 2026). Slovakia's status conflicts between sources. Development history: launched in 2009 with a Brazilian Air Force development contract reported at $1.3 billion, a two-year delay announced in July 2015 over budget cuts and the currency, and first delivery in 2019. The Brazilian order was later cut and stretched to 19 aircraft by 2034.
findings.source_title: Wikipedia: List of Embraer C-390 Millennium orders and deliveries; Axios (UAE); The Aviationist (Greece); AIN (2015 delay)

findings.claim: South Korea chose the C-390 in December 2023 for its LTA-II programme over the C-130J and A400M, in a budget of about 710 billion won ($544 million) for an expected three aircraft, with local parts manufacturing and maintenance (MRO) commitments.
findings.detail: DAPA cited favourable industrial terms promising a large amount of work for Korean subcontractors. ASTG, EMK and Kencoa Aerospace signed MoUs to make C-390 parts, and DAPA signed a further defence-cooperation MoU with Embraer in October 2025. Embraer said at the Singapore Airshow (3 February 2026) that it would deliver to the Korean Air Force by the end of 2026, and Lee inspected the first aircraft in July 2026. This defence work is the base the civil talks build on.
findings.source_title: Korea Times: S. Korea selects Embraer's C-390; National Defense Magazine; The Defense Post

findings.claim: Embraer's eVTOL unit Eve flew its full-scale prototype for the first time in December 2025 and now targets certification and entry into service in 2027, a year later than first planned.
findings.detail: Eve reports nearly 3,000 pre-orders (non-binding letters of intent) and plans six conforming prototypes for certification.
findings.source_title: Military Aerospace / Reuters via TravelDailyNews: Eve completes first flight of full-scale eVTOL prototype

findings.claim: Brazil's state already finances Embraer heavily, mostly export credit rather than development money: BNDES-approved financing for Embraer reached R$28.7 billion by January 2026.
findings.detail: On 12 February 2025, at a Nova Industria Brasil ceremony with Lula, Embraer announced about R$20 billion (about $3.5 billion) of investment in Brazil to 2030, alongside BNDES R$2.1 billion for E175 sales to Republic and Finep R$331 million for innovation. BNDES approved a R$279 million R&D loan on 14 April 2026. No source ties BNDES or the Brazilian treasury to funding a new narrowbody.
findings.source_title: Mercado e Consumo: Financiamentos aprovados pelo BNDES a Embraer alcancam R$28,7 bi; Folha PE; Agencia Infra

findings.claim: India's Adani Defence & Aerospace and Embraer signed an MoU on 27 January 2026 for an Indian final assembly line for regional jets (E175/E2), with Dholera in Gujarat chosen as the site in June 2026. Embraer has reportedly made the line conditional on about 200 firm Indian orders.
findings.detail: This is a regional-jet production partnership, not a narrowbody development partnership. Separately, in October 2026 Embraer proposed producing 48 C-390s in India with Mahindra.
findings.source_title: Aviation Week: Embraer Signals Indian Final Assembly Line Under Adani MOU; Outlook Business; MercoPress

findings.claim: Korea's space and aerospace agency KASA launched a public-private task force for international joint development of civil aircraft on 16 July 2026, aiming for Korean firms to become core partners in the Airbus/Boeing next-generation single-aisle programmes expected to start around 2030.
findings.detail: The task force is chaired by the KASA administrator and includes the presidential office, the industry ministry (MOTIE), the SME, foreign affairs and financial services ministries, KAI, Korean Air and Hanwha Aerospace. The model is for Korean firms to lead development of core parts or modules and win long-term exclusive supply rights in production, expected to give 20-30 years of steady volume. Some reports say development could start in 2028. The government also plans to expand production capacity and secure investment funding. The task force is aimed mainly at Airbus and Boeing, and Embraer is a parallel track.
findings.source_title: Newscj (Cheonji Ilbo) / Herald Economy: KASA civil aircraft international joint development task force

findings.claim: Korea's presidential office set a target of up to 135 trillion won of orders over 20 years from 2035 through international co-development of civil aircraft, and a Korean consortium of about 100 companies led by Hanwha Aerospace, Korean Air and KAI is being formed.
findings.detail: The 135 trillion won target was reported on 17 July 2026 and the consortium by KED Global on 15 July 2026. KASA's 2026 work plan lists winning a risk-and-revenue-sharing partner role in international civil aircraft development as a goal. No budget for the task force was found.
findings.source_title: Nate News: Cheong Wa Dae targets 135 trillion won orders; KED Global: S.Korea to form consortium to seek roles in commercial aircraft programs

findings.claim: Korea has no airliner engine programme: KASA and Hanwha Aerospace are developing a 4,500-lbf dual-use turbofan (90 billion won, to 2029) for drones and small aircraft, and Korea is separately funding an indigenous engine for the KF-21 fighter.
findings.detail: Hanwha says the small engine could be adapted for small business jets. It is far from a 25,000-30,000-lbf narrowbody engine. Hanwha is a risk-and-revenue-sharing partner on Pratt & Whitney's GTF engines since 2015, with reported shares of 1% (17,000-lbf), 3% (24,000-lbf) and 2% (30,000-lbf), and makes GTF parts. In May 2026 Korea's industry asked the government to join the WTO civil aircraft agreement, which could limit subsidies and local-content rules.
findings.source_title: UPI: Hanwha Aerospace begins Korea's first dual-use turbofan engine project; Hanwha press release (GTF RRSP); Seoul Economic Daily (WTO)

findings.claim: KAI is a mid-sized, mostly defence aerospace company (2025 revenue 3.696 trillion won, about $2.6 billion; operating profit 269.2 billion won) with long-running civil aerostructure contracts for both Boeing and Airbus.
findings.detail: Civil contracts: A320 wing bottom panels ($1.2 billion for 2014-2025, up to about $1.7 billion if extended to 2030, signed 2012); 737NG wing structures since 2004; exclusive 777X wing-rib supplier to 2030; A350-900/1000 wing main ribs; and a June 2025 Collins deal for A350/A320neo nacelle parts from 2027 (about 140 billion won). Hanwha raised its KAI stake to 15.89% in July-August 2026. KAI's top shareholder said in October 2026 it had no plan to sell, which complicates a Hanwha takeover.
findings.source_title: Nasdaq/RTT: Korea Aerospace Industries FY25 Profit Rises; Korea Times (2012 Airbus contract, 2025 Collins deal); KED Global

findings.claim: Korean Air's aerospace division is the sole supplier of A320neo sharklets, makes 787 aft-fuselage composite parts and wingtips, makes A350 cargo doors, and holds a new four-year Boeing contract from 2025 for 737, 767, 777 and 787 fuselage and wing structures.
findings.detail: Korea would therefore bring proven aerostructure factories in Sacheon and Busan, a composites skill base, Hanwha engine-part capability, and state money (KASA, Korea Eximbank and the presidential office's push). It would not bring airframe-integration or certification experience. A 2012 Bombardier-Korean consortium plan for a 90-seat turboprop did not go ahead. A 2010 Korean pre-feasibility study for an 88-seat turboprop assumed a $2 billion development bill with Korea paying 40% ($800 million).
findings.source_title: ch-aviation: Korean Air secures Boeing parts contract; Korea JoongAng Daily; KISTEP 2010 pre-feasibility report

findings.claim: Korea's home narrowbody market is largely committed to Boeing into the 2030s: Korean Air finalised a 103-aircraft Boeing order on 16 September 2026, including 50 737-10s (plus 20 777-9s, 25 787-10s and 8 777-8Fs).
findings.detail: The commitment was first announced in August 2025. Korean Air plans to standardise on 777, 787, 737, A350 and A321neo after integrating Asiana. A Korean home-market launch order for an Embraer-Korea narrowbody would therefore be small or late.
findings.source_title: Boeing News Release: Boeing, Korean Air Announce Record 103 Airplane Order

findings.claim: Benchmark for a third Western single-aisle maker: the A220 (ex-C Series, launched 2008, in service 2016) had 1,107 firm orders and 550 deliveries by September 2026, and production is still ramping to about 12-13 a month, with Airbus saying 14 a month is needed to break even.
findings.detail: A220 production was about 7-8 a month in 2025. Airbus set 12 a month as the 2026 target and is aiming for 13 a month by 2028. For scale, the A320neo family backlog alone was 7,493 in May 2026. Analysts and Faury cite Bombardier's near-collapse on the C Series as the warning case for Embraer.
findings.source_title: Wikipedia: List of Airbus A220 orders and deliveries; The Star/Reuters on A220 ramp (Oct 2025); Forecast International (May 2026 backlog)

model_inputs.name: Probability that Embraer (with Korean partners) launches a 150-200 seat narrowbody by 2032
model_inputs.basis: My judgement. Against a launch: the CEO has repeatedly said there is no concrete plan, product definition only starts from 2030, and any launch depends on mature engines and safe funding (EMB-9, EMB-11, EMB-12). Embraer cancelled the turboprop when engines and partners were missing (EMB-13), and the decision reportedly divides Embraer internally (EMB-15). For a launch: the Korean state is now pushing hard (EMB-1, EMB-2, KOR-1, KOR-2), there is a signed KAI MoU (EMB-3), and the CEO says there is room for 3-4 makers (EMB-14). Korea's talks are 'very early stage' and Korea's main track is joining Airbus/Boeing (KOR-1), which keeps the base below 0.5.

model_inputs.name: Entry into service year of an Embraer-Korea narrowbody (if launched)
model_inputs.basis: Product definition starts from 2030 (EMB-11). KASA expects international programmes to start around 2030, some reports say 2028 (KOR-1). Airbus picks its engine in 2027, launches around 2030 and targets service in 2037-38 (EMB-18), and Embraer will wait for mature engines (EMB-12, EMB-13). Embraer's history is about 5 years from launch to service for the E-Jet (EMB-24) and the E2 derivative (EMB-25); a clean-sheet 150-200 seater with a new engine and a new partner is more like the A220's 8 years (ANA-1). Launch 2029-2033 plus 7-10 years gives 2036-2043, base 2039. The game's generic entrant (2040) sits close to this base.

model_inputs.name: Peak production rate of the Embraer-Korea narrowbody
model_inputs.basis: Embraer's all-time commercial peak is about 100-130 a year, or 9-11 a month (EMB-23). Its 2030 capacity target for all commercial jets is 110-120 a year, about 10 a month (EMB-22). The A220, the closest analog, was at 7-8 a month nine years after service entry and is targeting 12-13 (ANA-1). Korea adds aerostructure factories (KOR-4, KOR-5) and could host a second assembly line, which drives the high case of 16. The game's generic 20 a month by 2046 is above every analog found.

model_inputs.name: Years from entry into service to peak rate
model_inputs.basis: The first-generation E-Jet reached about 10 a month around three years after its 2004 service entry, in a boom and for a smaller aircraft (EMB-23, EMB-24). The E2, in service since 2018, was still at only 44 deliveries in 2025 (EMB-22, EMB-25). The A220 has not reached its 14 a month break-even rate ten years after service entry (ANA-1). Supply-chain limits, especially engines, are Embraer's main ramp constraint today (EMB-22).

model_inputs.name: Embraer-Korea share of new single-aisle (150-200 seat) customers outside China, with a new Boeing airplane in service
model_inputs.unit: % of orders by units in years it is on offer
model_inputs.basis: In this world three modern Western types compete (Airbus NGSA, Boeing fps, Embraer-Korea). The benchmarks for a newcomer are the A220's 1,107 orders over about 18 years against an A320neo backlog of 7,493 (ANA-1) and the E2's roughly 500 firm orders in 13 years (EMB-25). Korea's home market is largely locked into the 737-10 (KOR-6), so Korea gives little guaranteed demand. Cap the share by capacity: peak_rate x 12 divided by the game's non-China single-aisle demand per year.

model_inputs.name: Embraer-Korea share of new single-aisle (150-200 seat) customers outside China, without a new Boeing airplane (737 MAX phasing out from 2045)
model_inputs.unit: % of orders by units in years it is on offer
model_inputs.basis: Without a new Boeing airplane, Embraer-Korea becomes the only non-Airbus Western alternative as the MAX ages out, and airlines and lessors that want a second source would split between Airbus and Embraer. This fits the CEO's 'room for 3-4 makers' argument (EMB-14) and the long Airbus/Boeing waits that already favour Embraer (EMB-15). It is limited by Embraer's capacity (peak 10 a month base) and by Embraer having no record in this segment (EMB-19, ANA-1). The high case assumes a second assembly line and a customer base that includes Boeing's former customers.

model_inputs.name: Development bill of an Embraer-Korea 150-200 seat narrowbody (programme total, all partners)

research.summary: Embraer has not launched or committed to a 737/A320-class airliner. Since 2024 its CEO, Francisco Gomes Neto, has said Embraer is 'making studies' but has 'no concrete plans', will start defining new products from 2030, and will launch only when supplier engine technology is mature and the funding does not put the company at risk. Embraer showed how seriously it means that by cancelling its turboprop in November 2025. The Korea partnership is real but early: Lula's February 2026 state visit to Seoul and Lee Jae Myung's July 2026 visit to Brazil put a jointly developed next-generation airliner on both governments' agendas. KAI and Embraer signed a non-binding civil aviation and aerostructures MoU on 28 July 2026, signed by KAI's Kim Jong-chool and Gomes Neto. Korea's policy chief Kim Yong-beom called the talks 'very early stage', with no agreed form or terms; the 150-200 seat range comes from the Korean side. Korea's main track is to become a core risk-sharing partner on the Airbus/Boeing successors from about 2030, through a KASA-led task force launched on 16 July 2026 with KAI, Korean Air and Hanwha Aerospace. Embraer is a parallel option. Other partners (Saudi PIF, Japan, Turkey, India) appear only in 2024-2025 reports from unnamed sources; India's Adani deal covers regional-jet assembly, not a new narrowbody. Embraer is a credible but small developer: E-Jet and E2 each took about five years from launch to service, the E2 on a $1.7bn budget; C-390 sales are growing (62 orders, many NATO buyers, Korea since 2023). The company has $7.6bn revenue, a $35.7bn backlog and an $11-13bn market value. Its commercial output peaks at about 9-11 jets a month, with a target of 110-120 a year by 2030. Industry and press estimates put a narrowbody at about $10bn (Korean press: about 15 trillion won), which Embraer cannot fund alone. Korea would bring aerostructure factories, composites and engine-part know-how, and state money, but no integration experience, no airliner engine, and a home airline already committed to 50 737-10s. For the model I suggest treating an Embraer-Korea airliner as a probability-weighted entrant: about 35% chance of launch by 2032, service entry around 2039, a peak of about 10 a month reached about 8 years after service entry, about 6% of non-China single-aisle orders if Boeing has a new airplane and about 14% if it does not, and a development bill of about $12bn, about 30% of it Korean.

verify.inputs_review:
Overall the ranges point the right way but lean optimistic, and the Korea-side evidence behind them could not be checked in this pass (see the gaps above).

1) Launch probability by 2032 (0.15 / 0.35 / 0.60). The base is too high for a launch of a specifically 150-200 seat narrowbody. Embraer's latest primary statement (8 May 2026) says the segment is undecided between a commercial jet and a business jet, there is no timeline, timing depends on outside technology, and funding must not risk the company's finances. In November 2025 the CEO said a new commercial product could be larger or smaller than the E195-E2. Embraer also refused to self-fund KC-390 development and cancelled the turboprop. The Korean link is a non-binding MoU plus 'very early stage' talks, and both are unverified here. Suggest low 0.08, base 0.20, high 0.40. Define 'launch' as board approval with a launch customer and committed partners.

2) Entry-into-service year (2036 / 2039 / 2043). Defensible, but skewed early. Embraer's own launch-to-service record is about 5 years for the E2 (June 2013 to April 2018). The KC-390, a clean sheet funded by government, took about 10 years (2009 to 2019) with reprogramming. If Embraer waits for next-generation engines, it is unlikely to enter service before Airbus's NGSA (2037-38, itself unverified here). Suggest 2037 / 2040 / 2044.

3) Peak rate (5 / 10 / 16 a month). Embraer's documented peak is 101-108 E-Jets a year (2015-2017), and its target is 120 commercial jets a year by about 2030 across all E-Jets. A new line sharing that industrial base makes 10 a month a stretch base. Suggest 4 / 8 / 14, keeping 16 only for a confirmed second (Korean) assembly line.

4) Years from service entry to peak (5 / 8 / 12). Reasonable. Embraer itself says commercial production levelling slips to 2027-28 because of 'pacer' suppliers.

5) Share with a new Boeing airplane (2 / 6 / 10 %). Reasonable. AirAsia choosing the A220 shows that incumbents with bundles and slots win even against a good third-maker product.

6) Share without a new Boeing airplane (6 / 14 / 25 %). The base and high cases break the finding's own capacity cap. At 8-10 a month (about 100-120 a year), share is capped at about 100-120 divided by the game's non-China single-aisle demand. Suggest 5 / 9 / 18, with the high case allowed only with a second line. Slot scarcity (Finnair: no MAX/neo positions until about 2032-33) supports some upside.

7) Development bill ($8bn / $12bn / $20bn). Every source behind the $10bn anchor (EMB-15, EMB-16, EMB-17) is unverified press, so the range is weakly grounded. Embraer also reports investment net of supplier contributions, so the E2's $1.7bn understates the programme total. State clearly whether the input is the programme total or Embraer's net share. Raise the low to about $10bn and keep $20bn+ as a C-Series-style overrun case. The gap to Boeing's $60-65B mostly reflects scope and should not be read as a cost advantage.

8) Korean share of the bill (15 / 30 / 40 %). Plausible, but rests on an unverified 2010 study and press reports. Add a zero-share case (Korea joins the Airbus/Boeing successors instead, its stated main track) by making the share conditional on the Korea-Embraer deal happening at all.

findings.source_title: FlightGlobal: Embraer lobbies to remove 10% US import tariff; GlobalAir: Embraer warns of order delays; Poder360

findings.claim: An executive order of 20 November 2025 (EO 14361) took the 40% Brazil tariff off beef, coffee, cocoa, fruit and other farm goods, backdated to 13 November 2025.
findings.detail: The updated Annex I lists 238 HTSUS lines and 11 farm categories. It came after a 6 October 2025 phone call and the 26 October 2025 meeting in Kuala Lumpur. Lula called it 'a victory for dialogue, diplomacy, and common sense.' The order did not touch the personal sanctions.
findings.source_title: C.H. Robinson client advisory 11-24-2025; Fortune: Trump removes Brazil tariffs on coffee

findings.claim: On 20 February 2026 the Supreme Court ruled 6-3 in Learning Resources v. Trump that IEEPA does not authorize tariffs. The Brazil 40% ended, and a 10% global tariff under Section 122 replaced the IEEPA duties from 24 February 2026, with civil aircraft exempt.
findings.detail: CBP stopped collecting the Brazil IEEPA tariffs around 22 February 2026. Vice-President Alckmin said about 22% of Brazil's US exports had still faced the 40% at that point. Section 122 allows 150 days, so the tariff ran to 24 July 2026. The administration said it meant to raise it to 15%; I did not confirm whether it did. Civil aircraft, engines and parts that qualify under the 1979 Agreement on Trade in Civil Aircraft were exempt, so Brazilian aircraft went from 10% to 0%. Aircraft were Brazil's third-largest export to the US in 2024 and 2025.
findings.source_title: DLA Piper: US Supreme Court holds IEEPA does not authorize tariffs; Covington: IEEPA tariffs terminated, replacement Section 122 tariffs take effect; AIN: Aircraft exempt from new tariffs

findings.claim: Embraer is getting refunds of the IEEPA tariffs it paid in 2025 and the first half of 2026. It says the tariff costs tied to its backlog are over.
findings.detail: A summary of the Q2 2026 call says Embraer booked about $8M of US import tariffs in the quarter and expects about $12M a year of indirect tariff costs, mainly in Services & Support. Tariff refunds and a $68M one-off tax credit lifted Executive Aviation margins. The CFO said Embraer is 'done with the tariff costs from the backlog.' CBP began processing refunds in May 2026, on application.
findings.source_title: Yahoo Finance: Embraer SA (EMBJ) Q2 2026 Earnings Call Highlights

findings.claim: On 15 July 2025, at the President's direction, USTR opened a Section 301 investigation of Brazil.
findings.detail: The Federal Register notice (90 FR 34069) ran on 18 July 2025. It covered six areas: digital trade and electronic payments (Pix), preferential tariffs, anti-corruption enforcement, intellectual property, ethanol market access, and illegal deforestation.
findings.source_title: Forbes Brasil: EUA investigam práticas comerciais do Brasil, Pix e etanol na mira

findings.claim: On 1 June 2026 USTR found Brazil's practices actionable under Section 301 and proposed a 25% tariff. The draft exemption annex included roughly 430 HTS lines that apply only to civil aircraft.
findings.detail: Its findings included the central bank's double role as regulator and operator of Pix, and ethanol: US ethanol exports to Brazil fell from $761M in 2018 to $96M in 2025. Counts of exempt lines differ: Green Worldwide says about 1,200 in total, others say more than 1,600. Global Trade Alert counts 546 'Aircraft' subheadings worth $2.6bn and models them at an effective 2.5%. Comments were due 1 July 2026.
findings.source_title: Green Worldwide: USTR proposes 25% Section 301 tariff on Brazilian goods, 430 aircraft carve-outs; Global Trade Alert; GHY

findings.claim: USTR announced final Section 301 action on 15 July 2026: a 25% tariff on most Brazilian goods from 22 July 2026. Civil aircraft, engines, parts and simulators are excluded, which covers Embraer.
findings.detail: Besides civil aircraft (all aircraft except military, with engines, parts, components, subassemblies and ground flight simulators), the exclusions cover beef, orange juice, energy, pharmaceuticals and goods already under Section 232. The exemptions reportedly cover about 44% of Brazil's exports to the US. The tariff adds to MFN duties. General Counsel Jennifer Thornton signed it. The Rio Times and a later analysis say it was still in force at the October 2026 election.
findings.source_title: USTR Fact Sheet: President Trump Directs USTR Section 301 Action in Response to Brazil's Unreasonable Acts, Policies, and Practices; Greenberg Traurig alert

findings.claim: Since 24 July 2026 Brazil has also faced a 12.5% tariff from a separate forced-labour Section 301 action covering 60 economies. Civil aircraft are exempt from it everywhere.
findings.detail: This action replaced the expiring Section 122 tariffs. Brazil's National Confederation of Industry says 4,060 Brazilian products are covered and 48.7% of Brazil's US-bound exports face some extra tariff. The Brazilian government expects the 12.5% and the 25% to stack, to 37.5%. Civil aircraft, engines, parts, components, subassemblies and simulators under HTSUS General Note 6 are universally exempt.
findings.source_title: C.H. Robinson: New Section 301 Forced Labor Tariffs Now In Effect; O Povo; MercoPress

findings.claim: A proclamation of 9 July 2026 ended the Section 232 investigation of commercial aircraft, jet engines and parts. It found that imports 'threaten to impair the national security' but imposed no tariffs and ordered negotiations, with a progress update due by 5 January 2027.
findings.detail: Commerce opened the investigation on 1 May 2025 (published 9 May, Federal Register notice 13 May 2025). The Commerce Secretary advised against immediate tariffs. The President may impose tariffs or other import limits if negotiations fail. This keeps a ready-made legal route for taxing foreign airliners.
findings.source_title: White House: Adjusting Imports of Commercial Aircraft, Jet Engines, and Aircraft and Engine Parts into the United States; International Trade Insights

findings.claim: In its Section 232 comments, Embraer argued that the US has 'never produced regional aircraft' and that its jets 'obviously do not threaten to impair US national security'.
findings.detail: Embraer's US defence rests on not competing with a US-built product. That argument would not hold for a 737/A320-class narrowbody that competes head-on with Boeing. Source is a public-comment summary in FlightGlobal; filing date not confirmed (mid-2025).
findings.source_title: FlightGlobal: China joins aerospace firms in urging no new US trade barriers

findings.claim: On 18 July 2025 Secretary of State Rubio revoked the US visas of Justice Alexandre de Moraes, his immediate family and his 'allies on the court'.
findings.detail: Rubio called the Bolsonaro case a 'persecution and censorship complex.' Jurist reported that 8 of Brazil's 11 Supreme Court justices were affected: Moraes, Barroso, Toffoli, Zanin, Dino, Cármen Lúcia, Fachin and Gilmar Mendes. The official statement used only the general 'allies' wording. No 2026 source found on whether these visa bans have been lifted.
findings.source_title: Jurist: US escalates Brazil tensions as Rubio revokes visas of judges involved in Bolsonaro case

findings.claim: Treasury put Global Magnitsky sanctions on Moraes on 30 July 2025, and in September 2025 added his wife Viviane Barci de Moraes and revoked more visas, including that of Solicitor-General Jorge Messias.
findings.detail: Treasury Secretary Bessent announced the July designation, which froze any US assets. Lula condemned the 'US government's interference in the Brazilian justice system.'
findings.source_title: WTOP/AP: Trump administration sanctions wife of Brazilian judge who sentenced Bolsonaro, revokes other visas

findings.claim: On 12 December 2025 OFAC took Moraes, his wife and the family-linked Lex Institute off the Magnitsky sanctions list.
findings.detail: Lula said he had asked for the delisting on a call with Trump. Human Rights First said the legally required notice to Congress was not given before the delisting. I did not open the OFAC notice; the date comes from multiple press reports.
findings.source_title: MercoPress: De Moraes and wife exit Magnitsky Act list; Bloomberg Law

findings.claim: The Financial Times reported on 16 August 2026 that the US government had discussed putting Magnitsky sanctions back on Moraes. No new sanctions were confirmed.
findings.detail: The report reportedly tied the talks to searches Moraes authorized in March 2026 against a journalist in Maranhão. It rests on unnamed sources, relayed by Reuters/The Star and Rio Times.
findings.source_title: The Star (Reuters): US considers new sanctions on Brazilian judge, FT reports

findings.claim: Trump and Lula met for about 45 to 50 minutes on 26 October 2025 at the ASEAN summit in Kuala Lumpur and set their teams to negotiate on the tariffs and sanctions.
findings.detail: Trump said 'I think we should be able to make some good deals for both countries.' Lula said a deal could come 'faster than anyone thinks.' Phone calls followed on 3 December 2025 (both sides called it 'productive') and in January 2026.
findings.source_title: RTHK: Trump, Lula hold 'positive' talks in Kuala Lumpur; Al Jazeera: Trump and Lula hold phone call (3 Dec 2025)

findings.claim: Lula's White House meeting on 7 May 2026 lasted about three hours. It produced a 30-day working group on the tariff dispute and the Section 301 case, but no deal.
findings.detail: Lula asked Trump to close the Section 301 investigation. On rare earths, Lula told Trump that Brazil would not sideline China or any buyer and that refining stays in Brazil. PIIE called it a 'meh meeting.' Six weeks later, in July 2026, USTR imposed the 25% tariff.
findings.source_title: PIIE: The Lula-Trump meh meeting; SCMP: Lula won't sideline China in rare earths; Planalto

findings.claim: Lula and Trump spoke by phone on 21 August 2026 about the new tariffs, and in August 2026 Brazil formally began examining retaliation under its reciprocity law.
findings.detail: Lula said negotiation was the best route. Trump proposed that officials meet as soon as possible. A Brazilian trade official called the reciprocity law 'an asset we're holding in reserve.' The Lula government accused the US of using forced labour as a pretext without legal basis.
findings.source_title: France 24/Reuters: Brazil's Lula urges tariffs resolution in call with Trump; Correio da Manhã: Governo Lula inicia processo de reciprocidade

findings.claim: In the first round on 4 October 2026, Senator Flávio Bolsonaro finished ahead of Lula, by 47.03% to 45.16% of valid votes. Neither passed 50%, so the race went to a run-off.
findings.detail: Turnout fell: abstention was about 21%, the highest since 1998. Flávio beat the final Datafolha poll by about 8 points. One Rio Times page gives 47.08%/45.11%; I treat 47.03/45.16 as the final TSE figures but did not open the TSE site.
findings.source_title: Rio Times: Brazil election first-round results; Wikipedia: 2026 Brazilian general election; Americas Quarterly

findings.claim: Lula won the 25 October 2026 run-off against Flávio Bolsonaro, with about 51.8% to 48.2%, for a fourth term.
findings.detail: Reported TSE counts: 51.79/48.21 with 99% counted; 51.76/48.24 with 99.77% of sections; 51.74/48.26 with 97.69%. It is the first time in Brazil that a candidate behind in the first round has won the run-off. Flávio called the result 'inexplicable' and said he would seek to annul it. The OAS observer mission, most foreign governments and most Brazilian political leaders recognized the result. Brazilian stocks fell after the result. One run-off report says the new term starts 5 January 2027.
findings.source_title: NPR: In stunning victory, Brazil's Lula wins fourth presidential term; CNN; Bloomberg

findings.claim: I found no statement from Trump on Lula's win. A CRS report cited by an analysis site says the administration had not recognized the re-election as of 28 October 2026.
findings.detail: Before the run-off Trump said he was 'monitoring' it and endorsed neither candidate, although he praised Flávio's first-round result and had hosted him in the Oval Office on 26 May 2026. The White House gave no immediate comment after the result. Reports say Flávio headed to the US after losing.
findings.source_title: Diplomacy & Law: Lula wins Brazil's runoff: will Trump escalate tariffs and sanctions?; Time

findings.claim: Xi Jinping sent Lula a congratulatory message on 27 October 2026. Lula's victory speech presented the win as a defeat for disinformation and foreign meddling.
findings.detail: Xi said he 'attaches great importance' to China-Brazil relations. Xi and Lula had also spoken by phone in January and on 27 July 2026; Xi called China and Brazil 'important members of the Global South.' Analysts (SCMP, China-Global South Project, Global Times) expect closer ties with China and BRICS. Time called the result a 'defeat for Trumpism.'
findings.source_title: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the PRC: Xi Jinping sends congratulatory message to Lula

findings.claim: Lula ran on national sovereignty against Trump's tariffs, sanctions and visa revocations, while saying he does not want Trump as an enemy.
findings.detail: He framed the Bolsonaro family's ties to Trump as a choice between independence and submission. He warned that China, the US and France would not get access to Brazil's minerals without respecting Brazilian sovereignty. In July 2026 posts he wrote that Brazil 'will not waver' in defending sovereignty. I found no Lula campaign pledge specifically on Embraer or on an Embraer narrowbody.
findings.source_title: Al Jazeera: Brazil's Lula launches fourth-term bid, focuses on national sovereignty

findings.claim: The losing candidate, Flávio Bolsonaro, lobbied USTR in July 2026 to postpone the 25% tariff and asked for Embraer aircraft and components to be excluded. He said Brazil should not have to choose between the US and China.
findings.detail: He testified at USTR's hearing and sent a formal request for postponement and bilateral talks. He blamed the tariffs on the Lula government's 'incompetence.' He reportedly backed a bill barring Pix from linking to 'non-Western' cross-border payment systems. He accused Lula of putting China first for ideological reasons.
findings.source_title: Band: Flávio Bolsonaro diz que tarifas beneficiam Lula e pede suspensão aos EUA; Diario de Pernambuco/AFP

findings.claim: Lula's government presents Embraer as a strategic national champion. On 12 February 2025, at a Planalto ceremony with Lula, Embraer announced R$20bn of investment in Brazil through 2030 under 'Mission 6' (sovereignty and defence technologies) of the Nova Indústria Brasil policy.
findings.detail: The money is for more aircraft production and new products, including eVTOL. That is about R$3.33bn a year over six years. The Lula government also pressed in 2025 for Embraer to be excluded from the US tariffs.
findings.source_title: Folha de Pernambuco: Governo Federal e Embraer anunciam R$20 bilhões em investimentos no Brasil até 2030; Forbes Brasil

findings.claim: Brazil's federal government holds a golden share in Embraer that can veto changes of control, name, purpose or logo, and decisions on military programmes and military technology transfer. Any holder reaching 35% of the capital needs government approval.
findings.detail: The veto list in the bylaws also covers training third parties in military technology and ending spare-parts supply for military aircraft. The golden share dates from the 1994 privatization and was kept intact in the 2006 restructuring. For the model: a Korean or other partner, or a Boeing tie-up, cannot take control without Brasília's consent.
findings.source_title: Embraer Investor Relations: Corporate governance model; By-laws

findings.claim: Brazil used that consent once: it approved Boeing's $4.2bn deal for 80% of Embraer's commercial business in January 2019, saying it would not use the veto. Boeing walked away in April 2020 and settled the arbitration for $150M in September 2024.
findings.detail: Embraer started arbitration on 27 April 2020. The settlement was a one-time $150M payment under a 'collar' agreement, below the market's expected ~$300M. A separate KC-390 joint venture (51% Embraer) was also dropped.
findings.source_title: ch-aviation: Boeing settles failed commercial aviation JV with Embraer; Engineering News (Jan 2019)

findings.claim: BNDES, Brazil's development bank, approved BRL 28.8bn for Embraer from 2023 to 2025. Of that, BRL 27.13bn financed exports of 169 aircraft. In August 2026 it approved up to R$3.7bn more for 19 E195-E2s for Canada's Porter.
findings.detail: The other BRL 1.68bn went to research and technology. The Porter loan is covered by the Export Guarantee Fund (FGE, run by ABGF), with deliveries through 2030; it is BNDES's first direct financing of Embraer exports to a Canadian airline. In December 2024 BNDES approved R$1.1bn for 8 jets for US lessor Azorra.
findings.source_title: bne IntelliNews: Brazil's BNDES steps up backing for Embraer; Datamar News: BNDES approves up to R$3.7bn for Porter

findings.claim: The WTO ruled in DS46, brought by Canada, that Brazil's PROEX aircraft export-financing programme was a prohibited export subsidy. Brazil later redesigned it (PROEX III), and that version was accepted.
findings.detail: The Appellate Body report was circulated 21 July 2000 and adopted 4 August 2000. A compliance panel found Brazil had not withdrawn the subsidies in time. Related cases: DS70 (Brazil v Canada, civil aircraft); DS222 (Brazil v Canada, export credits for regional jets, adopted 19 February 2002); and DS522 (Brazil v Canada over CSeries subsidies, filed 8 February 2017, still listed as pending, with the US, China and EU as third parties). The precedent caps how far Brazil can subsidize prices on an Embraer narrowbody.
findings.source_title: Wikipedia: Bombardier Aerospace and Embraer S.A. government subsidy controversy; USTR: Canada - Measures Concerning Trade in Commercial Aircraft

findings.claim: China took 28.7% of Brazil's exports in 2025 and the US 11.3%. Brazil-China trade hit a record US$171bn, more than twice Brazil-US trade.
findings.detail: Other counts put China at 28.3% to 29.3% depending on the period. Reporting ties part of the 2025 shift to the US tariffs.
findings.source_title: The Star: Brazil-China trade hits record US$171bil in 2025; Datamar News: China strengthens lead in Brazilian exports

findings.claim: Embraer's Harbin joint venture with AVIC subsidiaries (HEAI, reportedly 51% Embraer) closed in 2016, about 13 years after it opened.
findings.detail: It built ERJ-145 regional jets (about 50, from 2004 to about 2011) and then Legacy 650 business jets (2012 to 2016). The closure was announced 1 June 2016. Reasons given: weak demand, and Chinese tax rules that made imported aircraft cheaper than ones built in China. Embraer kept a Beijing office.
findings.source_title: AIN: Embraer to close Legacy 650 assembly facility in China; Aviation Week

findings.claim: COMAC's links to Brazil are thin. In 2024 the small carrier Total Linhas Aéreas discussed buying up to four C919s, but no order was confirmed and ANAC had not received a C919 certification request.
findings.detail: Financing of up to 80% from China Development Bank over 10 to 12 years was discussed. An analyst called it 'a very risky choice.' I found no 2025-2026 government-level aviation deal between Brazil and China.
findings.source_title: AJOT/Reuters: Brazilian airline seeks to buy planes from China's COMAC

findings.claim: Embraer's China airliner sales are modest: about 100 first-generation E-Jets, with few E2s.
findings.detail: A 20-E2 deal planned for Lula's 2023 China visit was delayed when Lula had pneumonia; Embraer later signed a deal to convert 20 aircraft to freighters in Lanzhou. Reports of the May 2025 Lula-Xi agreements mention Embraer jet purchases, but I could not confirm the numbers or types.
findings.source_title: FlightGlobal: Embraer targets Chinese E-Jet sales as Brazil and China tighten ties; Air Data News

findings.claim: Trump designated Brazil a Major Non-NATO Ally in 2019 (Presidential Determination 2019-21). I found no sign it has been revoked through the 2025-2026 dispute.
findings.detail: The designation is made under the Foreign Assistance Act and the Arms Export Control Act and was announced during Jair Bolsonaro's March 2019 visit. In October 2021 more than 60 members of Congress urged Biden to cancel it; an amendment that year by Rep. García to bar recognition of it was not shown as adopted. No 2025-2026 source confirms the current status either way.
findings.source_title: American Presidency Project: Memorandum on Designation of the Federative Republic of Brazil as a Major Non-NATO Ally

findings.claim: North America provided 58.7% of Embraer's US$7.6bn revenue in 2025.
findings.detail: North America was 59.1% in 2024. The rest of 2025: Europe 24.3%, Brazil 8.3%, Asia-Pacific 5.4%, Latin America outside Brazil 1.9%, other 1.4%. 96.6% of revenue is in US dollars.
findings.source_title: Embraer S.A. Form 20-F FY2025 (SEC EDGAR)

findings.claim: Major US carriers rely heavily on Embraer's E175, the only new-build regional jet that meets US pilot scope limits of 76 seats and 86,000 lb.
findings.detail: SkyWest ordered 60 firm E175s plus rights to 50 more at the 2025 Paris Air Show ($3.6bn at list price, deliveries from 2027). American ordered 90 firm plus 43 rights in March 2024. In July 2026 SkyWest had 68 E175s on firm order, 44 not yet assigned to a partner, flying for United, Alaska and Delta. Embraer's US customers are a constituency that pushes against tariffs.
findings.source_title: Aviation Week: Embraer unveils multiple regional jet orders; CAPA: SkyWest reports 69 planned E175 deliveries; Forecast International

findings.claim: In 2025 Embraer pledged $500M of US investment and aimed for 5,500 US jobs by 2030, but ruled out a US assembly line for E2 airliners.
findings.detail: Melbourne, Florida is its business-jet production and delivery base; a Dallas maintenance site was also announced. It plans $21bn of purchases from US suppliers and $13bn of exports to the US over five years. US-built KC-390s, with 2,500 more jobs, depend on a US government order.
findings.source_title: Air Data News: Embraer rules out E2 jet assembly in US over tariffs; Aviation Week: Embraer pledges $500M in US investment

findings.claim: After Boeing's April 2017 petition over Delta's order for 75 CS100s, the Commerce Department set a preliminary countervailing duty of 219.63% on the CSeries (26 September 2017) and a preliminary anti-dumping duty of 79.82% (6 October 2017).
findings.detail: The dumping margin used 'adverse facts available.' Reporting at the time said a duty near 300% would 'effectively disqualify' the jet from the US market.
findings.source_title: Leeham News: Decision was expected, tariff is a shocker in Boeing-Bombardier case; AIN: US hits Bombardier with new C Series duties

findings.claim: Commerce's final rulings of December 2017 set a combined duty of 292.21%: 212.39% countervailing plus 79.82% anti-dumping.
findings.detail: The duties could only be collected if the ITC found injury to Boeing.
findings.source_title: National Post (PressReader), 21 Dec 2017

findings.claim: On 26 January 2018 the ITC voted 4-0 that Boeing was neither injured nor threatened, which cancelled the 292% duties. Boeing let the appeal deadline of 22 March 2018 pass.
findings.detail: The ITC accepted that the CSeries and the 737-700/MAX 7 are in the same segment. But it found Boeing lost no sales or revenue on the Delta order, and the evidence on the United campaign was 'mixed.' Analysis said the outcome came down to seat count. Canada's foreign ministry said the matter was closed.
findings.source_title: AVweb: Boeing loses case against Bombardier; Global Affairs Canada statement (March 2018); FlightGlobal: Bombardier's trade court win came down to seat count

findings.claim: Airbus defused the duty threat by buying 50.01% of the CSeries programme (announced 16 October 2017) and assembling the A220 in Mobile, Alabama from August 2019, so that US-delivered jets count as domestic.
findings.detail: Bombardier's CEO said there is no import duty on 'a domestic product.' That the deal was meant to dodge duties is the press reading, not an official statement. A dedicated Mobile line followed. For Embraer and Korea the lesson is that US final assembly is a proven fix.
findings.source_title: FlightGlobal: Airbus to acquire majority share in CSeries programme; American Machinist: A220 assembly plant in Alabama completed

findings.claim: Korea Aerospace Industries and Embraer signed an MOU on aircraft structures on 28 July 2026. It names no narrowbody programme.
findings.detail: It covers research on new technology and manufacturing efficiency. Embraer's other Korean links are in defence: Korea chose the C-390, and the first Korean aircraft was in final assembly in February 2026. I found no confirmed Korean partner for a new Embraer single-aisle.
findings.source_title: Aju Press: KAI signs MOU with Embraer on aircraft structures; The Elec

findings.claim: Embraer has not launched a narrowbody. In 2026 it was making studies for a 'new cycle of products', and 2024 reports named possible partners in Saudi Arabia (PIF), Turkey, India and South Korea.
findings.detail: In 2024 the CEO said there were 'no concrete plans' for a big narrowbody. One 2026 analysis puts a clean-sheet single-aisle at $10-15bn and says even a 2026 launch could not reach volume production before 2035. Embraer has talked to all engine makers, including Rolls-Royce.
findings.source_title: Aviantics Labs: Embraer's narrow-body logic is sound, but its timeline has a ten-year problem; Leeham News (May 2024)

findings.claim: Korean Air committed to 103 Boeing aircraft, including 50 737-10s ($36.2bn at list price), at the Trump-Lee summit on 25-26 August 2025, and reportedly finalized the order on 16 September 2026.
findings.detail: The rest of the order: 20 777-9s, 25 787-10s and 8 777-8 freighters. Korea's trade ministry listed it among the agreements made at the summit. IBA estimates about $12.6bn at actual market prices. Korea's flag carrier is tied to Boeing through US-Korea trade politics, which limits how much Korean home demand a Korean partner would bring.
findings.source_title: Korea Times: Korean Air to purchase 103 Boeing planes following Korea-US summit

findings.claim: Boeing's 2025 Commercial Market Outlook forecasts 43,600 deliveries from 2025 to 2044, of which 33,285 are single-aisle.
findings.detail: The rest: 7,815 widebodies, 1,545 regional jets and 955 freighters. Single-aisle jets rise to 72% of the fleet by 2044, from 66% in 2024.
findings.source_title: Boeing 2025 CMO executive summary

findings.claim: Boeing's 2024 China outlook forecasts 8,830 deliveries to China through 2043, of which 6,720 are single-aisle.
findings.detail: 6,720 is about 20% of the global single-aisle total, comparing it with the 2025 global figure.
findings.source_title: ASD News: Boeing: China commercial fleet to more than double by 2043

findings.claim: Boeing's 2024 global outlook put North America at about 20% of 20-year deliveries, just behind Eurasia and China.
findings.detail: This share is for all deliveries, not single-aisle only, and comes from a secondary summary. I did not find a 2025 regional single-aisle table.
findings.source_title: Aviation Week: Boeing forecasts demand for nearly 44,000 new aircraft through 2043

model_inputs.name: P_us_formal_action_vs_embraer_korea_narrowbody
model_inputs.unit: probability (some US trade action filed or imposed against the jet between launch and 3 years after entry into service)
model_inputs.basis: BOM-1: Boeing filed against Bombardier within about a year of the first big US order (Delta). SEC232-1: since July 2026 there is a national-security finding against aircraft imports, with tariffs possible after January 2027. S301-1 to S301-3: the US was willing to target Brazil itself. SEC232-2: Embraer's 'US never made regional jets' defence fails for a 737 competitor. Pulling the other way: civil aircraft were exempted in all four 2025-26 tariff actions (TAR-1, TAR-4, S301-3, S301-4), and Embraer's US customers lobby against tariffs (US-3).

model_inputs.name: P_us_sustained_tariff_or_duty_ge10pct_at_EIS
model_inputs.unit: probability (a duty of 10% or more on the jet's US imports, lasting 2 years or more after entry into service)
model_inputs.basis: Embraer paid a 10% tariff for about 10 months in 2025-26 (TAR-2), but courts and later exemptions removed it (TAR-4). The ITC injury test struck down 292% duties in 2018 (BOM-3). The base is set above the Bombardier precedent because a 737/A320-class jet would take sales from Boeing directly; the ITC found no lost Boeing sales in the Delta case. It is set below 0.5 because a US final assembly line, as Airbus did in Mobile (BOM-4), or more US content (TAR-2: about 40% now) would largely neutralize duties.

model_inputs.name: P_us_market_effectively_blocked
model_inputs.unit: probability (duty above about 100%, or political exclusion, so the jet sells close to zero in the US)
model_inputs.basis: Commerce's 292% on Bombardier (BOM-1, BOM-2) was overturned 4-0 by the ITC and Boeing did not appeal (BOM-3). A block would need an injury finding plus no US-assembly workaround. Risk is raised by the Section 232 tariff route (SEC232-1), the US-Brazil rift with Lula re-elected (ELE-2, ELE-3, SAN-4), and Korean Air's Boeing commitments, which show Korea is politically tied to Boeing (KOR-3).

model_inputs.name: US_tariff_rate_if_taxed
model_inputs.unit: % ad valorem on the aircraft (or its non-US content)
model_inputs.basis: 10% was the 2025 IEEPA baseline and the 2026 Section 122 rate (TAR-2, TAR-4). 25% is the 2026 Brazil Section 301 rate (S301-3). 12.5% is the forced-labour 301 rate, which could stack to 37.5% (S301-4). 40% was the 2025 Brazil IEEPA add-on (TAR-1). The Bombardier 292% (BOM-2) is the tail beyond the high case, which the block probability covers.

model_inputs.name: P_embraer_korea_builds_US_final_assembly_if_threatened
model_inputs.basis: Airbus showed the route works (BOM-4). Embraer already has US plants and a $500M US investment pledge (US-4), and gets 58.7% of revenue from North America (US-2). Against: Embraer refused US E2 assembly in 2025 (US-4), and the golden share and Brazilian industrial policy (LEV-1, ELE-7) favour Brazilian work share. This is judgement.

model_inputs.name: world_single_aisle_demand_share_outside_China_and_US
model_inputs.basis: China has 6,720 of roughly 33,285 single-aisle jets, about 20% (MKT-1, MKT-2; the two figures come from 2024 and 2025 editions). North America is about 20% of all deliveries (MKT-3), and the US is most of North America. 1 - 0.20 - (about 0.17 to 0.20) gives roughly 0.60 to 0.63. The low case allows for China or the US taking a larger share.

model_inputs.name: politically_accessible_fraction_of_exUS_exChina_market

research.summary: US-Brazil relations fell apart in 2025 and are only partly repaired, but civil aircraft were consistently spared. The 40% IEEPA Brazil tariff of July 2025 exempted civil aircraft and parts, though Embraer paid the 10% baseline (about $2M a jet, about 90bp of margin) until the Supreme Court struck the IEEPA tariffs down on 20 February 2026. The Section 122 replacement, USTR's 25% Brazil tariff (effective 22 July 2026) and the 12.5% forced-labour tariff all exclude civil aircraft too. So Embraer now pays roughly zero on aircraft and is getting refunds. The personal sanctions eased: Moraes was taken off the Magnitsky list on 12 December 2025. But the FT reported in August 2026 that re-sanctioning him was discussed, and the May 2026 Lula-Trump meeting brought no deal. Lula won the 25 October 2026 run-off (about 51.8% to 48.2%) after trailing Flávio Bolsonaro in the first round (47.03% to 45.16%). He ran on sovereignty against Trump, and Xi quickly congratulated him. No Trump reaction or recognition was found, so more friction is likely, although Lula says he does not want Trump as an enemy. Brazil's levers over Embraer are strong: a golden share with veto over control (35% cap without approval) and military matters, and about R$9.6bn a year of BNDES financing, constrained by the WTO PROEX ruling. Brazil's economic tilt toward China is clear (28.7% of exports vs 11.3% to the US), but direct aviation links to China are weak (the Harbin joint venture closed in 2016; no COMAC deal). The Bombardier case shows both the threat and its limits. Commerce imposed 292% duties, the ITC cancelled them 4-0 because Boeing had lost no sale, and Airbus then made the jet 'domestic' with its Mobile, Alabama line. An Embraer-Korea 737-class jet would lose Embraer's 'US never made regional jets' defence and would face the July 2026 Section 232 aircraft finding, under which tariffs are still possible. My base case is therefore a 50% chance of some US action, 22% of a sustained duty of 10% or more, and 8% of an effective block, with US final assembly as the main way out. Even if blocked from the US, the jet could still reach about 60% of world single-aisle demand outside China and the US, against about 80% with the US open.
